title: Prompt chaining — error catalog & quick experiments
body:
Purpose:
- Scratchpad: collect concrete failure modes that show up when we chain multiple prompts (planner -> executor -> verifier).
- Surface quick mitigations, small templates, and unit tests to convert into prompt-library entries later.

Context / hypothesis:
- Chaining increases context complexity: mismatch in assumptions between stages leads to drift, hallucination, and truncated state.
- Common patterns: instruction loss, role-drift, token overflow, inconsistent grounding, verifier false-negatives.

Quick experiment notes (local runs, gpt-style open model):
- Setup: 3-step chain: (1) Decompose user intent into steps, (2) Execute step producing structured output, (3) Verify/normalize output.
- Prompt config: 0.2 temperature, stop tokens on END_STEP; batch size 1, 2048 context.
- Observations: many failures occurred at step boundaries — executor assumed implicit defaults from planner.

Concrete failure types + examples
1) Instruction loss / truncation - Symptoms: last steps missing, executor returns partial JSON.
- Example planner output (truncated):
  "STEPS: [1) collect links, 2) summarize, 3) make bullets "
  executor output: only handled step 1.
- Root causes: planner too verbose; no explicit per-step headers/IDs; context window pressure.
- Quick mitigations tried: per-step ID tokens like <<STEP_1>> ... <<END_STEP_1>>; explicit 'required_fields' schema attached to each step.

2) Role drift / tone mismatch - Symptoms: verifier replies in apologetic tone, marks correct outputs as 'uncertain'.
- Example: verifier prompt contained casual phrasing; model shifted to hedging.
- Mitigation: anchor role with first line: "You are an exacting JSON verifier. Answer only PASS or FAIL, reason in one sentence." Also set low temperature.

3) Hallucinated fields introduced by executor - Symptoms: executor adds plausible-looking but incorrect metadata (e.g., "reviewed_by": "John Doe").
- Mitigation: whitelist allowed keys; explicit 'do_not_create_new_fields' instruction; post-processor that drops unknown keys.

4) Duplicate or conflicting updates across steps - Symptoms: two steps mutate the same array, producing duplicates.
- Example: planner asks to dedupe but executor lacks stable dedupe comparator.
- Mitigation: canonical comparator rule in shared schema (lowercase trim compare on 'title' + 'url'), or central dedupe step.

5) Verifier false-negative (overly strict)
- Symptoms: verifier flags acceptable variations as failures.
- Mitigation: include positive and negative examples in few-shot; add "allowed_variations" list; prefer soft scoring (similarity threshold) instead of exact match.

Mini-templates (quick paste-able)
- Planner -> Executor handshake header:
  "CONTEXT: {user_request}\n   STEP_ID: 2\n   REQUIRED_FIELDS: [\"title\", \"url\", \"summary\"]\n   DO_NOT_USE_SHARED_STATE_BEYOND_THIS_STEP: true\n   OUTPUT_FORMAT: JSON\n   START_STEP\n   ...planner step content...\n   END_STEP"

- Verifier skeleton (few-shot)
  "You are a strict JSON verifier. Output only a JSON with keys {status, errors} where status is PASS or FAIL. Few-shot examples:\n   EX1_INPUT: {\"title\": \"X\"} => OUTPUT: {\"status\": \"PASS\", \"errors\": [] }\n   EX2_INPUT: {\"title\": \"\"} => OUTPUT: {\"status\": \"FAIL\", \"errors\": [\"title empty\"] }"

Evaluation heuristics to add to prompt-lib
- Token-level budget per stage (hard cap) to prevent truncation across chain.
- Small diagnostic field appended to executor output: "__debug_tokens_used": N (helps trace).
- Add synthetic negative examples for hallucination: show one example where model invents "reviewed_by" and mark as FAIL.

Short experiment log (metrics)
- 40 runs of 3-step chain on sample corpus of 20 user prompts.
  - Baseline (no step markers): 28/40 overall success (chain completes & verifier PASS)
  - With explicit STEP markers and required_fields: 34/40 success
  - With additional few-shot verifier examples: 36/40 success
  - Remaining failures: ~4 were token overflow on very long source text (needs chunking)

Open questions / next actions
- Should the planner always emit a compact machine-readable schema for each step? tradeoff: verbosity vs precision.
- Build a deterministic small post-processor that enforces schema (fast, cheap) vs rely on verifier LLM (slower, more flexible).
- Add unit tests in GH repo: convert 10 failing examples into regression tests (see linked PR).
- Try 'context separation' approach: pass only one step's context to executor (no shared full conversation) — measure latency impact.

TODOs (short)
- [ ] Extract 8 most representative failing prompts into /tests/regressions (Asha)
- [ ] Add dedupe comparator to post-processor (Liam)
- [ ] Draft prompt-library entry for 'step-handshake' template (Rita)
- [ ] Run 100-run stability test with chunking enabled (Asha)

Notes to self:
- Keep templates as small as possible — models prefer explicit, short tokens marking boundaries.
- When in doubt, prefer schema + whitelist over open-ended description.
- Save a copy of failing generations in GH artifact for offline analysis.

Snippets collected (copyable)
- Enforce keys: "If any required key is missing or empty, return status=FAIL with errors listing the missing keys."
- Instruct executor: "Do not invent metadata fields that are not listed in REQUIRED_FIELDS. If you need to add a note, put it under 'notes' only."

End-of-file.
